=== COLUMN 2 ===
The Old, The Very Old, The Very New
WALT CHERNOKAL PHOTO
Jimmy Clark, Duns, Scotland, in his sleek, low slung Lotus-Ford #92, brand new for the 1963 summer
racing season was lapping #21-John Pfrommer Sp. driven by Johnny White, Warren, Mich. and #7-Len Sutton,
Portland, Ore., the Leader Card Spl. White's mount was at least eight years old, Sutton's two years old. Neither
car stood a chance of beating Clark's speedy little mount. White tried hard but his mount just got tired and quit.
Sutton eased up and did finish the race. It was the 200 miler here last August.
HOT SCOT AND FRIEND
Jimmy Clark of Duns, Scotland
and his #92 Lotus-Ford will never be
forgotten by Milwaukee racing fans.
A truly great combination that hum-
bled one of the finest fields of cars and
drivers ever assembled.
Clark went on to win the world's
driving championship with one of the
most fearsome displays of speed and
handling ever seen here in America
or for that matter, anyplace else. The
field of drivers had no reason to be
LOTUSFord
ashamed in defeat. The 255 cubic inch
Ford engine built with a general Fair-
lane block employed all the latest
techniques to make the engine light-
weight, durable, and efficient.
The handling qualities of the car were truly remarkable. It didn't bounce over the little depressions in the
race track. It seemed to crawl over each low spot like a spider. It took builder Colin Chapman 13 years to get
his point across and he did it with absolute devastation at Milwaukee.

=== COLUMN 2 ===
It's a sad farewell we bid to Edward "Twenty
Grand" Steinbock, Chicago, who passed away Thurs-
day, April 23. Ed had been announcing races here
at state fair park since June, 1938. He was no new-
comer to racing. He drove a sprint car for a number
of years back in the 1920s on the tough northern
Illinois sprint car circuit. He earned the nickname
the same year "Twenty Grand" won the Kentucky
Derby. When he went through the fence in a race
and landed in a cornfield, somebody yelled, "Look
at old Twenty-Grand go for that corn."
"Twenty Grand" Steinbock was an announcer's
announcer. He kept meticulous records on all races
he covered. He knew racing from the ground up and
he could convey his knowledge. Auto racing will be
wanting because of his passing. He was a fine an-
nouncer, an excellent showman, and above all, a fine
gentleman.
Replacing "Twenty-Grand" is Myron Walden, a
staff announcer at WTMJ — The Milwaukee Journal.
Mike has been with the station since 1955. He's a
native of Springfield, Ill. and prior to coming here
was an announcer with the Illinois Sports Network
at Champaign.
Sports fans have heard Mike's broadcasts of
Green Bay Packer and University of Wisconsin foot-
5
ball; Milwaukee Braves baseball, and University of
Wisconsin basketball. While working for a small
station in Springfield, he handled a number of short
track broadcasting assignments. Mike's cheering sec-
tion is composed of wife, Nancy, and four youngsters
-Nanette, Greg, Julie, and David. The crew of
Wisconsin Auto Racing, Inc. welcomes you to state
fair park.
